sectionProgressions.progression: Single-note A walkup into A5 - C5 - D5
sectionProgressions.description: Fast-driving single note walkup answering the tambourine before stabbing into power chords
Muted percussive eighth-note rhythm with sudden dynamic stops
The classic rock double-plagal turnaround driving the anthemic vocal hook

harmonicFunction: A5 (I5) - The stomping garage rock home tonic
C5 (♭III5) - Blues-rock minor third power chord creating gritty push
D5 (IV5) - Subdominant chord completing the energetic riff cadence
G (♭VII) - Mixolydian subtonic chord that gives the chorus its triumphant pub rock drive

techniques.name: High-Tempo Motown Shuffle & Staccato Power Stabs
techniques.description: Strumming tight, palm-muted power chords at a blistering 205 BPM tempo, cutting off note decay instantly with fretting-hand mutes.

notes: Intro walkup: Open low E → fret 3 (G) → fret 4 (G#) → open A string
Power chords: A5 (fret 5 low E), C5 (fret 3 A), D5 (fret 5 A)
sequence: Lock into the tambourine and hi-hat beat on beats 2 and 4
Execute the chromatic walkup on the low strings
Stab the power chords cleanly with downstrokes
Choke all strings immediately on beat 4 for dramatic silence
tips: Keep your right-hand wrist loose: tense forearms will fatigue quickly at 205 BPM
Cameron Muncey used a Gibson Flying V through a cranked Marshall JCM800 for maximum Australian pub crunch
Honor every stop: the tight full-band rests make the song sound huge

techniques.name: Chuck Berry Double-Stops & Pub-Rock Lead Attack
techniques.description: Playing Cameron Muncey's raw, high-voltage garage-rock soloing in the 5th-position A blues scale, using simultaneous index-finger barre double stops on the high E and B strings, aggressive pick digging, and snappy bent thirds.

notes: 5th-position A minor pentatonic / blues box (frets 5 to 8)
Dual-string double stops at the 5th fret across strings 1 and 2
Bent 7th-fret G string (D up toward E) pushed with ring and middle fingers
Aggressive down-up alternate picking locked with Chris Cester's driving drums
sequence: Flatten your index finger across strings 1 and 2 at fret 5
Dig hard into the 7th fret of the G string and bend a whole step
Strike the double stop cleanly with a sharp downward brush
Descend aggressively through frets 7 and 5 on the D and A strings to resolve on the root A
tips: Channel Chuck Berry and Angus Young—keep the pick attack savage and dynamic
Use a heavy pick (1.0mm+) so it doesn't flex against the heavy strings at 205 BPM
Set the Marshall amp gain just high enough for natural bite without muddying note definition

sections.name: Tambourine Count-In & Chromatic Intro Riff
sections.description: One of the definitive guitar hooks of the 2000s garage rock revival, entering after Chris Cester's famous tambourine count-in.
notes: Fast chromatic bass walkup on low E and A strings
Staccato power chord stabs on A5, C5, and D5
Maintain relentless forward energy at 205 BPM

sections.name: Verse 1 Staccato Groove & Dynamic Drop
sections.description: Nic Cester's swaggering vocals ('1, 2, 3, take my hand and come with me...') over tight, chugged A5 power chords with abrupt full-band stops.
notes: Chug muted A5 on the low strings
Cut sound dead on the full-band stops
Keep right hand loose to avoid forearm cramping at 205 BPM

sections.name: Chorus 1 Double-Plagal Singalong ('Be My Girl')
sections.description: The soaring chorus 'So what you got to say? She's with me and I'm with her' built on the classic G - D - A rock turnaround.
notes: Full open chord strumming with maximum stadium power
Accent the rapid transition from G to D to A
Let the final A chord ring out before slamming back into the verse

sections.name: Verse 2 Rhythmic Build & Tambourine Drive
sections.description: The second verse intensifying the groove with driving eighth-note downstrokes and pick scrapes leading toward the explosive second chorus.
notes: Dig in with firmer pick velocity as the verse builds
Lock tight with Mark Wilson's driving bassline
Clean slide down into the chorus downbeat

sections.name: Cameron Muncey Fiery Blues-Rock Guitar Solo
sections.technique: Fast Chuck Berry Double-Stops & Minor Pentatonic Bends
sections.description: Cameron Muncey's raw, Chuck Berry-inspired blues-rock guitar solo in the 5th position, filled with howling bends and biting double-stops.
notes: 5th-position A minor pentatonic and blues box licks
Aggressive pick attack with natural tube saturation
Quick double-stops barred across the high E and B strings at fret 5

sections.name: Outro Frantic Jam & Stutter Stop Finish
sections.technique: High-Energy Riff Jam & Sudden Final Choke
sections.description: The breathless garage-rock finale where the riff cycles at maximum adrenaline before cutting dead on the legendary stutter-stop.
notes: Give every ounce of right-hand energy to the final riff cycles
Clean power chord transitions at 205 BPM
Execute the final stop instantly with zero string hangover

guitar.recommended: Gibson Flying V or Gibson ES-335
guitar.pickup: Bridge humbucker for biting garage-rock cut and high-mid punch

effects.distortion: Ibanez TS9 Tube Screamer (for solo boost)
effects.other: Heavy celluloid plectrums (1.0mm) for fast downstrokes

beginner.title: Chorus Chords & Rhythm
steps: Learn the open G, D, and A chords
Practice shifting between them at a comfortable 140 BPM
Build speed up to the album tempo of 205 BPM

intermediate.title: Main Riff & Staccato Mutes
steps: Learn the chromatic intro walkup on the low strings
Master the A5, C5, and D5 power chord stabs with clean hand mutes
Lock tightly with the fast drum beat without dragging or rushing

advanced.title: Solo & Full-Speed Endurance
steps: Learn Cameron Muncey's fast 5th-position blues solo note-for-note
Build right-hand stamina to play all 3.5 minutes at 205 BPM with zero tension
Perform live with authentic Australian pub rock swagger

commonMistakes: Tensing up the right forearm during the 205 BPM shuffle rhythm
Letting open strings ring during the silent stop-time pauses
Rushing ahead of the drum beat on the intro walkup
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Chromatic walkup at 150 BPM → 180 BPM → 205 BPM
5 minutes: Power chord staccato muting drill with metronome
focusAreas: Right-hand wrist relaxation at high tempo
Crisp silence on the stop-time chokes
metronomeWork: Start metronome at 160 BPM to ensure clean pick placement
Advance by 10 BPM increments to 205 BPM
